title: An expedition begins with a personal decision
conclusion: Gartina credits Nienna’s ship and crew with making the expedition possible.
limit: The speech does not make Nienna the sole restorer of Gael.

title: A fatal stand on the Plains of Trial
conclusion: Nienna stands before Saray against soul eaters and wraiths. She dies during the fight; Saray defeats the remaining enemies and brings her body to the Tower.
limit: Nienna’s warning to flee and Saray’s later guilt do not establish an objective allocation of blame or permanent destruction of Nienna’s soul.

title: Raise Dead at the Tower
conclusion: Saray obtains a diamond through an altar offering. Elenia casts Raise Dead, and Nienna wakes in alarm before being reassured by her friends.
limit: The spell record follows the awakening in posting order but documents the same return. This does not describe the separate September sacrifice.
previousLimit: The restoration mechanism and complete intervening scene remain unrecovered.

title: Time bought for the Hallowing
conclusion: Nienna turns toward the horde after her farewell. The later narration records the Hallowing completing and life expanding.
limit: The Hallowing does not establish a universal rule for sacrifice or resurrection.

title: Protection before the confrontation
conclusion: Adelia casts Death Ward on herself, Bitoshi and Elenia before the expedition continues.
limit: These targets are not an exclusive list of everyone protecting the party.

title: The labor of the Hallowing
conclusion: The narrator records the spell’s completion and names Adelia, Gartina and Elenia among those exhausted by sustaining it.
limit: The scene does not assign the entire restoration to one person.

title: Answering Jiangshi’s praise
conclusion: Jiangshi calls Adelia the true Hope in her eyes. Adelia answers that hope belongs to everyone.
limit: Later transformation does not retroactively turn either statement into exclusive authorship.

title: Memory becomes protection
conclusion: Elenia places Death Ward on Quake and explains that it saved her and Nienna. Quake thanks her.
limit: Her explanation is testimony about the earlier rescue, distinct from the visible casting.

title: Catastrophic harm and recovery work
conclusion: Wrath cleaves Elenia in two; Gartina rushes to recover her remains.
limit: The battle receipts alone do not establish a return; the subsequent Sanctum scene now supplies Gartina’s Reincarnate and its outcome.

title: Judgment and exile are separate events
conclusion: Bowene proposes a Crucible duel between Elenia and Magnus. In the later exile scene he names Elenia, Aravil and Olokun.
limit: These two receipts alone do not explain every cause of the later judgment.

title: Living ground is personally consequential
conclusion: Gartina weeps at the green ground and removes her boots to feel the grass.
limit: Her response is not evidence of sole authorship.

title: A staff, a tree and material help
conclusion: Gartina plants her staff; narration describes its pine transformation. Later she credits Krone’s limestone transport.
limit: The tree transformation does not by itself prove every forest effect permanent.

title: Choosing to remain
conclusion: Gartina says she wants to rejoin the others eventually but stays because refugees and the new forest need work.
limit: This statement does not record a resignation or a formal change in command.

title: A rescue remembered through failure
conclusion: Quake tells Dale that he and others died trying to rescue an ambushed company, while others succeeded.
limit: The speech is not a complete casualty list or a reconstruction of each rescue action.

title: A duty beyond defeating an enemy
conclusion: Quake answers that their duty is to protect the land and its people.
limit: A declaration of duty does not prove every later decision fulfilled it.

title: Receiving protection in return
conclusion: Elenia protects Quake with Death Ward, recalling earlier survival with Nienna; he thanks her.
limit: The protection is not a guarantee of survival or an explanation of every later return.

title: Bringing the means for Nienna’s return
conclusion: Saray survives the Plains fight and brings Nienna’s body home, then obtains a diamond through an altar offering. Elenia uses it to cast Raise Dead and restore Nienna.
limit: Saray’s guilt remains her self-assessment; the recovery does not establish that the guilt has ended.
previousLimit: The intervening return is not established by these two anchors.

title: A commitment inside the trial
conclusion: Saray accepts Dale’s proposal; Akarian directs that the rings go to Elenia.
limit: A decision about the rings is not a universal inheritance or ownership rule.

title: The final blow against Wrath
conclusion: Saray makes her last shot; the narration describes Wrath collapsing, and Scribonia observes her final blow.
limit: Victory does not explain the later return of every fallen companion.

title: Grief beneath the vigil
conclusion: Akarian describes making relics with Huoth and calls the company to a test.
limit: His description of the relics’ making remains his account.

title: An outcome of the test
conclusion: Akarian directs Draygar to give Elenia the rings.
limit: It does not establish permanent ownership of every relic.

title: Care and forward pressure coexist
conclusion: Akarian offers to take Sildithas’s watches, then agrees to push on.
limit: A single exchange does not establish an inflexible doctrine of advance or retreat.

title: Repair as a civic contribution
conclusion: Ryvyt describes following the wall builders and using Mending on their work.
limit: The account does not make him its only builder.

title: Skill needs a supply network
conclusion: Ryvyt asks for scouts to gather plants, relics and usable stone or metal.
limit: A request does not prove the materials were delivered.

title: A founder speaks after loss
conclusion: Ryvyt introduces himself as the remaining Ale-Chemy Knights founder; the post marks his hurt.
limit: Remaining does not independently determine the fate of every other founder.

title: Vital Chain in proposal form
conclusion: Fenwick shares a draft for coordinated medical care, public health and readiness in Eovar and Pristinia. He still speaks conditionally about opening branches.
limit: It does not date a legal founding or establish two completed branches.

title: An edited public notice
conclusion: A tower notice advertises the Silver Spire’s baths, market and healing house. It explicitly records a later July edit.
limit: The original posting timestamp cannot date every sentence of the edited text.

title: Writing for later travelers
conclusion: Fenwick frames his location guide as correctable notes and records a dangerous Plains visit.
limit: The casualty account is not automatically identical to every earlier Sildithas death.

title: A familiar place in the tavern
conclusion: Tobias returns to the Common Man with his silvered flail and sits down to order ale.
limit: The flail and the tavern scene alone do not establish an institutional rank or founding claim.

title: A welcome made practical
conclusion: Tobias offers food and directs Fredrick toward Herb’s rations.
limit: An offered meal does not establish an oath, recruitment or completed membership.

title: A town’s name meets its actual size
conclusion: Melian favors Pristinia while questioning John’s grander wording for a small settlement.
limit: The exchange does not establish a sole founder or erase the other participants.

title: Absence is discovered before its explanation
conclusion: Narration places Herb, Lillian and the raven dead near Melian’s open house, with Melian missing.
limit: The narrator places the event on the preceding day; the receipt’s posting date is not the abduction date.

title: Classifying a new settlement
conclusion: Scribonia records an early assessment and travel estimates attributed to the Master Librarian.
limit: His development rank and route estimates are not objective geography or an official town classification.

title: Achievement and self-doubt diverge
conclusion: During the relic trial Scribonia credits his students while judging his own accomplishments harshly.
limit: His claim of having accomplished nothing is not the archive’s historical verdict.

title: Remembering companions before the battle
conclusion: Scribonia deliberately takes in the support and relationships around him before facing Wrath.
limit: His description of the last Vanguard members is a contemporary perception, not an exhaustive roster.

title: An offer that wounds a relationship
conclusion: Wren offers herself if Wrath spares the others; Vaemyr hears this as standing alone again.
limit: The offer is not an accepted bargain, and neither perspective resolves the other.

title: Loyalty does not remove political doubt
conclusion: Wren weighs possible representatives and voices concerns about Magnus and Elenia.
limit: These are her concerns, not findings that settle another character’s motives.

title: Confidence from others
conclusion: Kasiri names Severina as someone she would follow during Kumai’s questions.
limit: An endorsement is not by itself a formal appointment.

title: Trial and leadership remain separate
conclusion: The contest outcome is recorded separately from Kumai’s wish to discuss leadership.
limit: No sole-founder claim or cleanly dated command transfer follows automatically.

title: Fear becomes a reason to investigate
conclusion: Sildithas argues that local fear of the Maw is a reason to go where help may be needed.
limit: The proposal does not establish what the Maw is.

title: Restoration remembered later
conclusion: Sildithas later attributes trees and forest to earlier restoration work.
limit: Retrospective credit supplements the direct December scenes rather than replacing them.

title: A crossing is not its explanation
conclusion: Coralyn separates the experience of losing magic from her theories about its cause.
limit: The note cannot establish the nature of the Maw, Chains or the entities around them.

title: Testing a route as a question
conclusion: Coralyn asks whether teleportation works beyond the Chains and discusses a place-linked item.
limit: A proposed means of travel does not prove that the crossing succeeded.

title: Recovery before expansion
conclusion: Rolen proposes a stealth-led mine operation, retrieving fallen friends before attempting a further search.
limit: This is a plan, not proof that every stage occurred.

title: Adapting to another person’s limits
conclusion: Rolen places an air genasi farther back while considering whether natural magic may be sensed.
limit: His hope about detection is not a confirmed rule of the mine.

title: Authority before the bereavement
conclusion: The narrator places High Lord Bowene beside Captain Zythienne in August.
limit: The accession mechanism and date remain unknown.

title: A decision inside the war council
conclusion: Bowene says the council will not pursue the proposed pact with Death.
limit: This decision is not a universal constitutional prohibition on every future pact.

title: Naming the exiles
conclusion: Bowene names Aravil, Olokun and Elenia while arranging their departure.
limit: Magnus is not named as an exile in this receipt.

title: Making a public case for authority
conclusion: Magnus addresses Zarathis by invoking what he says he has done beside its people and Aria.
limit: His speech is not independent corroboration of every service he lists.

title: Accepting the frame of the Crucible
conclusion: Bowene proposes a duel against Elenia; Magnus asks about preparation and timing.
limit: These opening receipts do not settle the later spell, duel result or entire exile rationale.

title: Restoring Nienna
conclusion: Elenia casts Raise Dead with the diamond Saray obtains, then embraces and reassures Nienna when she wakes in alarm.
limit: The spell record follows the awakening in posting order but documents the same return. This does not describe the separate September sacrifice.

title: Gartina calls her back
conclusion: Gartina casts Reincarnate in the Sanctum; the narrator records Elenia returning still a satyr.
limit: No higher-power cause is established; the full table behind the reported odds is not reproduced.

title: Risking change for a friend’s return
conclusion: Gartina prepares Elenia’s body and casts Reincarnate; Elenia emerges alive and still a satyr.
limit: The narrated outcome does not establish divine control over the rolls.

title: Retreat from the first creature
conclusion: Anky teleports himself and Alfred away and urges Cerwin to run after their portal has closed.
limit: His two-hour estimate does not fix map geometry.

title: The construct kills Anky and Alfred
conclusion: Anky urges Alfred to flee; Alfred refuses to leave him. Explicit narration then records the construct killing both and discarding their bodies across the Chains.
limit: This death scene does not prove that no later resurrection could occur.

title: The body is brought home
conclusion: Severina retrieves Thorn’s body; Ryvyt’s alchemical treatment removes the strange oil, and the party reaches the Tower.
limit: Removing the oil is not itself a resurrection.

title: An attempted restoration and a living recovery
conclusion: Alyhotep begins a Wish-based resurrection after Severina’s request. Thorn is alive and moving about the Tower by 8 September; Alyhotep asks about further healing.
limit: The precise moment of spell completion has no separate narrator confirmation in the checked excerpt.

title: Waking to another friend’s loss
conclusion: Elenia restores Dale at the Tower; he wakes beside Saray and learns that Nienna has died.
limit: The exact spell name is not established by these selected records.

title: A promise that leaves room for the survivor
conclusion: Dale and Saray discuss his changed music and promise that the survivor still has a life to live. He contributes to Nienna’s recovery effort.
limit: Their words do not establish that grief or self-blame is finished.

title: A return within the battle
conclusion: After Dale falls, Elenia reaches him with light; he returns to life and responds to Saray.
limit: The exact spell and a universal rule of revival are not established.

title: A future with music and a home
conclusion: Saray gives Dale a gift and speaks of hearing his music if he builds in Gael.
limit: The exchange does not establish a completed house or identify the gift’s magical properties.

title: Facing Wrath without feeling powerful
conclusion: Saray rejects Wrath’s blame of the world, then breaks down after he withdraws.
limit: This scene does not establish that every later action has one motive.

title: Continuing while grieving
conclusion: Saray calls on the company to keep fighting after Dale falls and later urges retreat; his return astonishes her.
limit: Continuing to act is not proof of completed emotional recovery.

title: Supporting Dale’s plans to build
conclusion: Saray gives Dale a gift and imagines hearing his music in Gael if he builds there.
limit: The house’s completion and gift’s properties are not established.

title: Learning silence under pressure
conclusion: Eugene studies the realm’s magic, sustains silence and uses written communication to help the company.
limit: The narrator’s local limit does not establish a universal spell or safe route.

title: A repaired conversation with Wren
conclusion: Wren and Eugene exchange apologies after her unexpected welcome.
limit: An apology does not establish that every cause or consequence is resolved.

title: A book for a complicated teacher
conclusion: Eugene and Olokun make a restrained memorial for Scribonia amid Zarathian hostility.
limit: The act does not independently resolve Scribonia’s full fate or the city’s accusations.

title: Accepting an institutional refusal
conclusion: Casimir accepts the consequences after Ephraith says he and Alioth chose each other and failed the trial.
limit: Alioth’s disagreement does not reverse the institutional outcome.

title: Offering work after a ruined concert
conclusion: Casimir checks on Alioth, offers help clearing the venue and argues for better payment for Carmen.
limit: The offer is not a completed cleanup or paid contract.

title: Shelter and a quieter plan
conclusion: Casimir brings companions under cover and proposes notes and concealment while the company needs silence.
limit: The scene does not establish permanent safety or complete geography.

title: Finding a route through reading
conclusion: Alioth organizes a social visit to the Rahu and draws on reading and local stories to find the embassy.
limit: The courteous cover does not establish full understanding or a lasting diplomatic success.

title: Disagreeing with the verdict
conclusion: Alioth calls loyalty to Casimir a strength after Ephraith declares their trial unsuccessful.
limit: The speech is her judgment, not an overturned verdict.

title: Offering care after the concert
conclusion: Alioth moves among the company offering healing, then checks on Casimir.
limit: The brief actions do not certify that every injury is healed.

title: Practical help in a dangerous silence
conclusion: Alioth offers to conceal tracks and writes in stone while the company needs silence.
limit: The realm’s identity and all outcomes of onward travel remain bounded by their evidence.

title: A mutual promise for the survivor
conclusion: Saray asks Dale to keep living if she dies. He asks the same of her, and she agrees to their mutual promise.
limit: The promise records their wishes; it does not establish that future grief will be simple or impose the same choice on anyone else.

title: The ward does not make a rescue simple
conclusion: Scribonia remains free of the mist’s visions, but Arjahn resists his portal and Wren’s attempted extraction also fails.
limit: The ward’s exact spell name and universal protections are not established by this packet.

title: A wide clearing, followed by collapse
conclusion: Scribonia uses Wish; the mist disperses, companions are released and Abyss withdraws. He later collapses and needs to be carried.
limit: The exact wish wording, duration, permanent mist state and universal spell cost remain unestablished.

title: A tether cannot withstand a believable family emergency
conclusion: Arjahn cuts his safety rope and pursues an apparent Sajhan, then becomes lost and paralyzed.
limit: The vision establishes neither a living Sajhan at this location nor the objective truth of Arjahn’s self-blame.

title: Refusal followed by an escort home
conclusion: Arjahn rejects Death’s offer after the vision and escorts the companions who are carrying Scribonia back.
limit: Neither the shared vision’s contents nor every claim about the family’s deaths is independently established here.

title: The protector also needs a rescuer
conclusion: Paralyzed and badly wounded by the salamander, Olokun depends on Ryvyt’s healing and restoration before helping kill it.
limit: His embarrassment is not a narrator judgment of his worth or ability.

title: Oya’s apparent danger and an offer refused
conclusion: The mist lures Olokun with an apparent illness threatening Oya. After release, he refuses Death’s offer involving her safety.
limit: Oya’s illness, Death’s protective promises and his claims about Aria remain unconfirmed.

title: A rescue interrupted by the lost-child vision
conclusion: Nymera tries to carry Olokun out, then releases him when the mist presents a lost child she calls Elyndra.
limit: The child’s present survival, location and complete history are not established by the vision.

title: Freed before the wider clearing, then carrying another
conclusion: Ryvyt’s Dispel Magic frees Nymera before the Wish; later she carries the exhausted Scribonia toward the refuge.
limit: Neither instant emotional recovery nor permanent healing of her burn marks is established.

title: The search becomes an apparent rescue of children
conclusion: Wren enters after the cut rope returns, then tries to protect apparent Shadar-kai children from a moth horror.
limit: The vision does not establish real deaths or children physically present in this part of Babel.

title: Anger and continued care coexist
conclusion: After Scribonia slaps her, Wren remains angry but helps gather the group, encourages Nymera and gives her food.
limit: The future resolution of the conflict with Scribonia is outside the snapshot.

title: Preparation keeps Olokun in the fight
conclusion: Ryvyt heals Olokun and uses Lesser Restoration after the salamander paralyzes and badly wounds him.
limit: This success treats the salamander’s paralysis, not every later effect in the mist.

title: A failed remedy followed by a successful dispelling
conclusion: Greater Restoration fails on Olokun, wind shifts the mist only briefly, and Dispel Magic frees Nymera before the Wish.
limit: The result does not establish blanket immunity or that either spell always succeeds or fails against every mist effect.
